title: Ordinary, Reasonable Chatbots: Do AI Models Track Human Legal Judgments?

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model responses to a 25-question legal reasonableness survey against the aggregate response profiles of men versus women using cosine similarity embeddings and regression analysis.

Comparing model responses to a 25-question legal reasonableness survey against the aggregate response profiles of white versus non-white human participants using cosine similarity embeddings and regression analysis.

Comparing model responses to a 25-question legal reasonableness survey against the aggregate response profiles of older (45+) versus younger (18-44) human participants using cosine similarity embeddings and regression analysis.

Evaluating educational bias by comparing model responses to a legal reasonableness survey against the aggregate response profiles of individuals with a bachelor's degree or higher versus those with an associate's degree or less.

Comparing the central tendencies (medians) of model-generated numerical estimates on legal scenarios against human baselines to identify systematic pro-government or pro-corporation leanings (e.g., longer warrantless tracking, lower safety spending).
